title: Sloppy Joes
subtitle: Sweet and tangy minced beef in a soft burger bun
excerpt: Beef mince cooked in a sweet, tangy tomato and pepper sauce, piled into soft burger buns until it falls out the sides. A classic American school-dinner sandwich.
sourceNotes: Classic Midwestern American sandwich with roots in 1930s diners and school cafeterias.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the beef mixture in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in a covered pan.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the mixture and freeze half in portions. The sauce gets better with a longer simmer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling a day ahead. It reheats well and the flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: Sloppy Joes are a loose, saucy beef mince filling piled into soft buns until the sauce runs down your hands. They give a sweet, tangy, deeply savoury plateful. Make the filling thick enough to stay in the bun when you first spoon it in, since it loosens as it sits.
Cook the beef mince in the dry frying pan over a high heat. Break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes until browned. Drain off any excess fat.
Add the onion and green pepper. Cook for 4 minutes over a medium heat until softened.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ketchup, tomato puree, and Worcestershire sauce. Add the mustard, brown sugar, cider vinegar, and a splash of water. Stir well.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened and coats the meat.
Season with salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust the sweet-sour balance with more sugar or vinegar.
Pile generously into the toasted buns and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The filling is too watery and falls out of the bun.
items.cause: The sauce was not reduced enough.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered until the mixture looks thick and jammy. It should hold its shape briefly when spooned.

items.cause: Not enough seasoning or the tangy elements are out of balance.
items.fix: Taste after adding the sauce. Add more Worcestershire for depth or a small splash more vinegar for brightness.
Always toast the cut sides of the buns in a dry frying pan. It takes 1 minute and makes a real difference.
